tool: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.15 in print mode, run in an empty directory outside the repository: `agy -p "<request>" --model gemini-4-neon-high --mode accept-edits --sandbox --output-format json`. The agent hands the request to its built-in image-generator subagent, which writes the image prompt and calls its generate_image tool.
model: gemini-3.1-flash-image behind generate_image (the service named it in a capacity error of the same session; the tool does not report it on success); agent gemini-4-neon-high; image-generator subagent gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high.
prompt: A photorealistic seamless tileable flat texture of brushed stainless steel metal, viewed straight-on from directly above, filling the whole frame edge to edge. Fine straight horizontal hairline brush lines and a few faint micro-scratches on cool silver-grey metal. Completely flat, uniform, even diffuse lighting across the entire square frame with consistent brightness and detail from center to edges.
request: Generate exactly one image with aspect ratio 1:1 and nothing else. Image description: A seamless tileable surface texture of brushed stainless steel: fine uniform straight horizontal hairline brush grain and a few faint micro scratches on a cool silver-grey metal, viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic, top-down), completely flat even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no perspective, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings, uniform detail across the whole frame so it can tile seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, square.
postProcessing: 1. ImageMagick 7.1.2-36, a one-off conversion of the generated JPEG to an 8-bit RGB PNG: `magick source.jpg -strip -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor PNG24:source.png`. 2. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts prepare brushed-metal source.png`: the last 128 columns and rows are cross-faded into the first ones (seamless, 896x896), the broad light and shade is removed (a wrapping box blur of radius 112 subtracted, the mean kept), and the image is area-averaged to 512x512. 3. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` writes normal.png, roughness.png and metalness.png from basecolor.png.
